{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Enoch Beery Seitz.jpeg|thumb|Enoch Beery Seitz]]
'''Enoch Beery Seitz''' (1846 - 1883)<ref name="Andrews">{{cite web|publisher=School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of St Andrews|title=Enoch Beery Seitz|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Seitz.html|place=Scotland|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref> was an American mathematician who was Chair of Mathematics at [[Truman State University|North Missouri State Normal School]] (now know as Truman State University).  


Enoch Berry Seitz was born 24 August 1846 in [[Fairfield County, Ohio]].
 
Seitz was elected to the [[London Mathematical Society]] on 11 March 1880, only the fifth American to be so honored.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=1 |issue=1|title=Biography: E. B. Seitz |url=https://archive.org/details/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_1894-01_1_1/page/n1 |date=January 1894|last=Finkel|first=Benjamin F|pages=3–6 |jstor=2968643|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|doi=10.2307/2968643}}</ref>{{rp|3–6}}  Over 500 of his solutions<ref name="Andrews" /> were published in the ''Analyst'', the ''Mathematical Visitor'', the ''Mathematical Magazine'', the ''School Visitor'' and the ''Educational Times'' of London, England.<ref name="Herald">{{cite news|title=Enoch B Seitz Was a Teacher of The Great|newspaper=The Herald-Advertiser|place=Huntington, West Virginia|date=8 October 1933|last=Hall|first=R C}}</ref>

He died 8 October 1883 at [[Adair, Missouri]]
